reader_notes: Read by hand from the note text (dump.ts, bars 1-23), independently: no external analysis consulted. x = the right hand's sixteenth line 1:1.25-3:2.75 (D4 E4 F#4 G4 A4 Bb4 G4 A4, G4 F#4 E4 D4, the seventh leap to C5, falling to G4; then the falling one-beat sequence D5 C5 Bb4 D5 / C5 Bb4 A4 C5 and the rising Bb4 ... E5): ten beats. y = the bass's counterline from 1:1 to 2:4.5: G2, then a chromatic descent G3 F#3 F3 E3 Eb3 D3 decorated by neighbour sixteenths (F#3 G3 A3 G3; E3 F3 G3 F3), ending D3 G3 F#3. y-INV = its exact (real) melodic inversion, first in the right hand 3:4.5-5:1 (D5 Eb5 E5 F5 F#5 G5 rising, with Eb5 D5 C5 D5 and F5 E5 D5 E5 as neighbour groups). 'x-body' = x from its second beat (G A Bb G A G F# E D, seventh leap, C Bb A), used on its own in sequences. openings.ts found the canon at 3:1.25 correctly.

leader.material: x (against y in the bass from 1:1: the piece starts with the two lines together)

first_imitation.changes: modal: F3 for F#4 (3:3.5) and Eb3 for E4 (4:1.5), the lowered seventh and sixth; the last note Bb3 (5:2.75) for E5, turning to the cadence. Otherwise exact to 5:2.5.

opening.leader_meanwhile: exchange with inversion: the leader takes over the bass's counterline y, but melodically inverted (y-INV, real), from 3:4.5; it stands two beats later against x than y did, so the pair is not a strict double-counterpoint exchange.
opening.canon_strict_to: 5:2.5 (the follower copies x only; it is not a canon beyond the first statement)
opening.notes: Two-voice texture from the first beat: x and y are stated together, so the bass is the follower for x but itself a thematic line from 1:1.

members.reason: x in the bass from 7:1.25 (A2 B2 C#3 D3 ...), y in the right hand from 7:2.75 (C#5 D5 E5 D5, C#5 C5, B4 C5 D5 C5, B4 Bb4, A4 D5 C#5), exact; y's first note G is replaced by F5 held and a run G5 A5 Bb5. Thirds become sixths: invertible at the octave. Continued in bars 9-10 (see elaborations).

members.reason: Tonic return, voices as in the prime: x in the right hand at 18:3.25 at the original pitch (D4 E4 F#4 ...), y in the bass at its original pitch with F#3 G3 A3 G3 at 19:1 aligned with x as in bar 1. Changes: y's head is Bb3 held and a run C4 D4 Eb4 instead of G2 and G3; x has Eb4 for E4 (19:3.5); x's falling sequence is extended by one unit (20:3-20:4.75) and its last rising figure becomes a scale to the cadence (bar 21).

members.reason: x in the right hand at 13:1.25 (G4 A4 B4 C5 D5 Eb5 ..., complete to 15:2.75 with Bb4 and Ab4 for the raised degrees, as in the prime's follower), y-INV in the bass from 13:3 (B2 G2 . G2, Ab2 G2 F2 G2 Ab2 A2, Bb2 A2 G2 A2 Bb2 B2, C3), placed against x exactly as in the prime. The bass's 13:1-2.75 (Eb3 D3 C3 D3 Eb3 F3 G3 Ab3) is the end-of-x figure the prime has in the right hand at 3:1. Then the bass takes x itself in c (15:1.25, true head, seventh leap G2-F3) where the prime's right hand had the varied x-body, against cadential leaping eighths in the right hand; the prime's second unit (to d) is cut and the member closes with a PAC in c at 16:3.

layout.form: rounded bipartite (first part 1-11 ends with a PAC in the minor dominant; the second goes to c and returns to alpha in the tonic at 18:3). Alternative: tripartite 1-7 / 7-16 / 16-23, taking the IAC at 7:1 as the first division, since bar 7 begins with alpha in a new key.

also: canonic opening (bars 3-5 only, too short for the canonic kind)

notes: Sure: x and y stated together from bar 1; the canon of x at the octave below; y-INV as the leader's counterpoint; the exchanged returns of alpha (d, 7) and beta (c, 13); the tonic return at 18:3; the four cadences at 7, 11, 16, 23 (7:1 less sure). Unsure: whether bars 5-6 belong to beta's prime or are elaboration (they are kept in beta because their pattern, x-body against leaping eighths, returns exchanged in 15-16); the form (rounded bipartite vs tripartite). Passing arrival on Bb (III) at 6:1 (bass F2-Bb2, right hand on D5, mid-sequence) is not counted as a cadence. The answer's Eb and F naturals give the canon a subdominant colour; the tonic return keeps one of them (Eb4 at 19:3.5).
